options.metric: Annual number of motorist deaths reported in NYC motor vehicle crashes, summed from number_of_motorist_killed.
options.denominator: None; this is a count, not a rate.
options.grouping: Calendar year derived from crash_date, 2013-2025 inclusive.
options.reason: A direct annual fatality count is a defensible measure of the reported burden even though it cannot measure per-mile risk.
options.answer: This file cannot establish whether risk per mile declined; the annual count of motorists reported killed fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025, although it fluctuated sharply in between.
options.interpretation: For calendar years 2013-2025, this sums number_of_motorist_killed across all police-reported NYC motor vehicle crash records; the count was 110 in 2013 and 81 in 2025, with a peak of 139 in 2020. This is defensible as the direct annual fatality burden, but it is a count with no exposure denominator. It leaves unanswered whether risk per mile declined because the file contains no vehicle-miles-traveled or other mileage exposure. Checks found 0 missing motorist-deaths values among 2,132,218 source crash rows and observed dates spanning January 1 to December 31 in every year; I kept all rows, with none dropped or counted differently, and found no checked sentinel dates.

options.metric: Annual number of police-reported NYC crashes with at least one motorist reported killed (number_of_motorist_killed > 0).
options.denominator: None; this is a crash count, not a rate.
options.grouping: Calendar year derived from crash_date, 2013-2025 inclusive.
options.reason: Counting fatal crash events is a defensible way to track how often a reported crash involved a motorist death, separate from how many people died per event.
options.answer: This file cannot establish whether risk per mile declined; crashes with at least one motorist killed fell from 102 in 2013 to 75 in 2025, despite intervening increases.
options.interpretation: For each calendar year 2013-2025, this counts police-reported NYC crash records whose number_of_motorist_killed value is greater than zero; the count was 102 in 2013 and 75 in 2025, rising in some intervening years. This is a defensible event-count framing because a crash with multiple motorist deaths still counts as one fatal crash. It leaves unanswered whether risk per mile declined and does not measure the number of motorists killed, because the file has no mileage exposure and the metric counts crashes. Checks found 0 missing motorist-deaths values among 2,132,218 source crash rows and observed dates spanning January 1 to December 31 in every year; I kept the full source cohort for classification, with no rows removed for missing values, and found no checked sentinel dates.

options.metric: Annual share of NYC police-reported crashes with at least one motorist reported killed (number_of_motorist_killed > 0) among crashes with a non-missing motorist-deaths field.
options.denominator: All police-reported NYC crashes in the same year with a non-missing number_of_motorist_killed value.
options.grouping: Calendar year derived from crash_date, 2013-2025 inclusive.
options.reason: The share of crashes involving a motorist death is a defensible crash-severity measure that adjusts the fatal-crash count for the number of reported crashes.
options.answer: This file cannot establish whether risk per mile declined; the share of crashes involving a motorist death rose from 0.0501% in 2013 to 0.0877% in 2025.
options.interpretation: For each calendar year 2013-2025, this divides crashes with number_of_motorist_killed greater than zero by all police-reported NYC crashes with a non-missing motorist-deaths field; the share rose from 0.0501% in 2013 to 0.0877% in 2025. This is a defensible crash-severity framing because its denominator is all reported crashes in the same year, rather than an unadjusted event count. It leaves unanswered whether an individual motorist's risk per mile declined, since it conditions on crashes and the file contains no mileage exposure. Checks found 0 missing motorist-deaths values among 2,132,218 source crash rows, so the known-field denominator excludes 0 rows; every year had observed dates from January 1 through December 31, and I kept all rows with no separate missing group or checked sentinel dates.
